{{Short description|French physicist (1931–2023)}}
'''Michel Gaudin''' (2 December 1931 – 4 August 2023) was a French physicist, known for the [[Gaudin model]], in which a central spin is coupled to many surrounding spins.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Feigin, Boris|authorlink=Boris Feigin|author2=Frenkel, Edward|authorlink2=Edward Frenkel|author3=Reshetikhin, Nikolai|authorlink3=Nicolai Reshetikhin|title=Gaudin Model, Bethe Ansatz and Critical Level|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=166|issue=1|pages=27–62|year=1994|arxiv=hep-th/9402022|doi=10.1007/BF02099300|bibcode=1994CMaPh.166...27F|s2cid=17099900 }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Michel Gaudin was born on 2 December 1931.<ref name="BNF">{{cite web |title=Gaudin, Michel (1931-....) forme internationale |url=https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb12313528n.public |website=BnF |access-date=23 December 2023}}</ref> After graduating with the degree of ''ingénieur des ponts et chaussées'' (civil engineer), Gaudin joined in 1956 the [[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique|CEA]] in [[Saclay]] to work on neutron experiments. Two years later, he joined [[Claude Bloch]]'s theorists' working group, to which he belonged for the rest of his career.<ref name="ForewordModeles">{{cite book | title = Foreword in: '' Modèles exactement résolus'' | author = M. Gaudin | publisher = | location = | year = 1995}}</ref> In 1967 he received from the [[University of Paris-Sud]] in Orsay his doctoral degree in physics with thesis ''Étude d'un modèle à une dimension pour un système de fermions en interaction''.<ref name=BNF/> Gaudin's research deals with, among other topics, the quantum-mechanical description of many-body systems, in particular, spin systems.

With [[Madan Lal Mehta|M. L. Mehta]] in 1960 he published ''On the density of eigenvalues of a random matrix'', an important paper on [[random matrix|random matrices]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Mehta, Madan Lal|author2=Gaudin, Michel|title=On the density of eigenvalues of a random matrix|journal=Nuclear Physics|volume=18|year=1960|pages=420–427|doi=10.1016/0029-5582(60)90414-4|bibcode=1960NucPh..18..420M}}</ref>

Gaudin received the Fondation Saintour Prize, awarded every two years since 1889 by the [[Collège de France]].<ref>{{cite journal| title = Fondation Saintour | journal = L'Annuaire du Collège de France. Cours et Travaux | issue = 109 | pages = 59–71 | author = Collège de France | url = https://journals.openedition.org/annuaire-cdf/pdf/226| doi = 10.4000/annuaire-cdf.226 | date = March 2010 | url-access = subscription }}</ref> In 2019, he received, with two other physicists, the [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]] from the [[American Physical Society]].

Gaudin died on 4 August 2023, at the age of 91.<ref>{{cite news |title=Michel Gaudin 1931–2023 |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/michel-gaudin-1931-2023/ |access-date=23 December 2023 |publisher=CERN Courier |date=9 November 2023}}</ref>
